title: Burke Substance Vocabulary — 18 substance types from GM-02 + scattered elaborations
primary_source: GM-02 (Part 1.II Antinomies of Definition); GM-01 also engages substance-grammar at ratio-interfaces; GM-06 Aquinas/Aristotle treatment elaborates actus/status pair.
purpose: Catalog of substance-types Burke uses as the dialectical machinery underlying the pentad. Each entry: operational gloss ≤80 words; Burke's primary example; the dialectical move the type enables; cross-link to pentad term.
content_filter_compliance: All Burke prose paraphrased; no ≥25-word verbatim.

substance_types.label: Paradox of substance (general)
substance_types.gloss: The structural irony at the root of all substance-talk: the word designates what a thing intrinsically is, but etymologically refers to something outside the thing that stands beneath or supports it. Every substance-claim therefore covertly imports a contextual reference into an intrinsic claim.
substance_types.burke_paradigm_example: Locke's 'something I know not what'; tortoise-supporting-the-elephant regress (GM-02 p.22).
substance_types.dialectical_move: Master-irony from which the chapter's taxonomy derives — every substance-claim oscillates between intrinsic and extrinsic poles.

substance_types.label: Contextual (positional, geometric, definitional) substance
substance_types.gloss: Definition by placement of a thing within its context, location, or surroundings. To define is to mark boundaries (de-finire), and to mark boundaries requires reference to what is outside the thing. Maximalist version: Spinoza's universal substance where each object is determined by the totality (omnis determinatio est negatio).
substance_types.burke_paradigm_example: Spinoza on substance and nature/God; Southern Agrarians *I'll Take My Stand* as a stand 'in Dixie' (GM-02 pp.24-25).
substance_types.dialectical_move: Treats the thing as 'in terms of' its scene; intrinsic / extrinsic swap places at the boundary; pairs like heredity/environment, mind/matter take one term as the other's 'context.'

substance_types.label: Geometric substance
substance_types.gloss: Subspecies of contextual substance: object placed in its setting via logical-spatial relations from which everything else is 'necessarily' derivable; Euclidean-Spinozistic implicit-relation calculus. Plastic enough to slide into materialist determinism.
substance_types.burke_paradigm_example: Spinoza's geometric method; Dreiser's view of motives as 'chemism' (GM-02 p.29).
substance_types.dialectical_move: Reduces motive to inevitable derivations within a closed scenic totality; dialectical antinomy is that 'necessity' here is purchased by erasing the agent.

substance_types.label: Familial (tribal, ancestral) substance
substance_types.gloss: Defining a substance by ancestral cause — biological descent or any 'spiritualized' analogue (covenant, founder, eponym, creation). Includes Plato's archetypal forms (each thing imitating its eponym in heaven) and Aristotle's entelechy (the individual as actualization of its class).
substance_types.burke_paradigm_example: Christian derivation of humanity from God; Plato's theory of forms; Nazi blood-philosophy; cluster 'general/generic/genetic/genitive' (GM-02 pp.26-28).
substance_types.dialectical_move: Stresses derivation rather than placement; mediaeval universalia debate (ante rem / in re / post rem) is its dialectical-realist/Aristotelian/nominalist refraction.

substance_types.label: Directional substance
substance_types.gloss: Substance characterized by motion toward, by 'the way,' by direction-from-within. Strongly futuristic and purposive ('Where are you going?' rather than 'Where are you from?'). Includes the cluster motion/movement/cause/emotion/moment as variant glosses on motivation.
substance_types.burke_paradigm_example: Tendencies, trends; immigrants as part of a 'westward movement'; I.A. Richards's pun on emotion as motion (GM-02 pp.31-32).
substance_types.dialectical_move: Converts 'free' motion into determined motion via statistical regularity; reveals substantial paradox in 'tendency' (a tendency to do X is by the same token a tendency not to do X).

substance_types.label: Nutritive (transubstantial) substance
substance_types.gloss: Merger of contextual and familial substance grounded in consumption of external elements that become internal — eating as transubstantiation. The organism's environment becomes its consubstantiality.
substance_types.burke_paradigm_example: Eucharist; totemic rites; Coates's *Eater of Darkness*; manganese as 'mother love chemical' (GM-02 pp.30-31).
substance_types.dialectical_move: Dissolves morphological boundary between organism and environment (Angyal's biosphere; Bernard's 'internal environment').

substance_types.label: Dialectic substance
substance_types.gloss: The over-all category: substance arising from systematic contemplation of the antinomies — recognition that we necessarily define a thing in terms of something else, where the something else is not merely an other but the other (the antagonist, the agon). Dramatistic super-category that covers the rest.
substance_types.burke_paradigm_example: Agon in tragedy and politics; Coleridge's 'rivales as opposite banks of the same stream'; 'we become the image of the thing we hate' (GM-02 pp.33-34).
substance_types.dialectical_move: Treats motive in terms of verbal/symbolic action; cultural accretions of language become a 'second nature' intrinsic to agents as agents.

substance_types.label: Substance under the paradox of purity (pure substance)
substance_types.gloss: When a substance is purified by abstraction to its absolute, it tends toward its negation: God as 'pure person' is impersonal; pure being is not-being; pure escape is perpetual imprisonment in escape; class-motive becomes pure when set against the individual.
substance_types.burke_paradigm_example: Plotinus's negative theology (One reached by negating the material); Hegel's pure being / not-being; Aristotle's Pure Act = eternal repose (GM-02 pp.35-37).
substance_types.dialectical_move: Identifies an asymptote where any term, intensified to absolute purity, flips into its dialectical antithesis — the formal engine of negative theology.

substance_types.label: Divisive (split) substance
substance_types.gloss: Subspecies of the paradox of purity: the agent is divided into 'two substances' by competing motivational scenes — typically a collective/universal scene against an individual scene. The same person acts under one substance qua patriot and another qua individual.
substance_types.burke_paradigm_example: Soldier killing nationally but not individually; the man with one substance at work and another at home as 'split personality' (GM-02 p.37).
substance_types.dialectical_move: Names the formal mechanism by which an agent is multiply substantial, anchoring later analyses of identification and ideology.

substance_types.label: Tragic-dialectic substance (poiēma / pathēma / mathēma)
substance_types.gloss: Substance constituted through the tragic triad: act (poiēma) calls forth a counter-assertion from its context which the agent suffers (pathēma); from the suffered comes knowledge (mathēma) that transcends the original act. Substance here is what is left when act, suffering, and learning fuse into character.
substance_types.burke_paradigm_example: Greek proverb *ta pathēmata mathēmata*; Galileo's experimental 'ordeal'; Hegelian succession of self-realizations.
substance_types.dialectical_move: Couples act-agent ratio to the dramatistic-temporal structure of trial-suffering-insight; provides the formal grammar for any tragic motive-analysis.

substance_types.label: Actus / status substance (act and state)
substance_types.gloss: Dyadic reduction of the tragic triad: act vs. state, motion vs. rest, drama vs. lyric, faith-as-act vs. knowledge-as-state. Maps onto potentiality/actuality; tracks the philological transformation by which active terms (aretē, virtus, hero) drift into states of being or sheer negations.
substance_types.burke_paradigm_example: Aretē/virtus from Ares — 'prowess' to potentiality to state of mind to not-killing; hero from doer-of-deeds to inherited reputation; kingship from heroic act to inheritable state — 'L'état c'est moi' (GM-02 pp.41-43).
substance_types.dialectical_move: Maps directly onto the Act-Agent ratio: where the chapter's substance vocabulary articulates with the pentad most tightly. Class-substance follows by the same logic.

substance_types.label: Class (occupational) substance
substance_types.gloss: Sociological refraction of actus/status: occupational acts develop characteristic properties; over time these properties harden into class-defining states. Ruling classes pass from a regime in which act and status are co-balanced into one where inherited position eclipses any continuing act.
substance_types.burke_paradigm_example: Nobility derived from horsemanship-in-war turning to pageantry and sport; kingship becoming sheer inheritable state (GM-02 p.42).
substance_types.dialectical_move: Anchors actus/status sociologically; provides formal grammar for diagnosing the petrification of action into property.

substance_types.label: Universal motive as substance (the One God / Gold Standard)
substance_types.gloss: When a substance becomes a universal motive, it operates as a master scene supplying all believers with a common motivational ground. Monotheism and the monetary motive are structurally parallel; both let agents traverse local scenes without losing identity (hypostasis preserved).
substance_types.burke_paradigm_example: Universal religion / Stoic cosmopolitanism / British imperial 'dressing for dinner'; monetary motive shadowing monotheistic motive (GM-02 pp.43-45).
substance_types.dialectical_move: Universal motives are 'incipiently' polytheistic — they must split into adjectival sub-motives ('saints,' 'nationalisms,' 'wage slavery' vs. 'capital') to handle the diversity of local scenes; Marxism applies this to the factory.

substance_types.label: Intrinsic / extrinsic substance
substance_types.gloss: Dialectical pairing of motivations-within-the-agent against motivations-derived-from-scene. Hegel pairs Matter (extrinsic, gravity-externally-referred) with Spirit (intrinsic, Bei-sich-selbst-sein). Poles invert structurally when an intrinsic principle is operationalized through external means.
substance_types.burke_paradigm_example: Hegel on Matter and Spirit; Korzybski's 'inside-the-skin / outside-the-skin'; gerontologist's 'intrinsic resistance to disease' (GM-02 pp.46-49).
substance_types.dialectical_move: Whenever this distinction is present, paradoxes of substance follow. Spinoza's *causa sui* marks the limit: humanism makes man *causa sui*; supernaturalism derives human substance from God as ancestor.

substance_types.label: Rhetorical substance
substance_types.gloss: The ambiguity of substance as a deployable resource of persuasion. 'Substantially,' 'essentially,' 'in principle,' 'in the long run' — adverbs that allow a speaker to assert a thing's identity at a level of generality that cannot be falsified by particulars. Positivists who outlaw substance reimport it covertly under 'in-principle.'
substance_types.burke_paradigm_example: Slave 'substantially free'; petition ruled 'substantially fraudulent' then reversed; League of Nations accepting proposals 'in principle' (GM-02 pp.51-53).
substance_types.dialectical_move: Locates the rhetoric of substantiation as a working tactic in legal, political, and scientific discourse — including disciplines that disavow substance.

substance_types.label: Substance as point of departure (consistent / compensatory)
substance_types.gloss: Because pentad terms function as 'principles' with overlapping margins, a thinker uses a substance-term as a point of departure in two opposite manners: (i) consistently, deriving consequences from its nature; (ii) compensatorily, departing from the term toward its near-antithesis. The god-term retains its rhetorical anchor while the structure built under its name actually moves elsewhere.
substance_types.burke_paradigm_example: 'Naturalism' begun as man-in-nature, becoming a name for technology-and-money; 'personalism' affirming persons where persons are not paramount; Descartes giving 'new proofs of the existence of God' that subtly redefine God (GM-02 pp.53-55).
substance_types.dialectical_move: Identifies the diachronic mechanism by which a substance-term's content evolves without changing its name — load-bearing for any historical diagnostic of philosophical idiom-shift.
substance_types.related_pentad_term: all five (any term can be a god-term)

substance_types.label: Consubstantial substance (epithetic, identificatory)
substance_types.gloss: Substance as it operates in epithets and identification-tactics: to call a man brother is to proclaim consubstantiality with him; to call him bastard is to attack his familial authorship. An epithet assigns substance doubly — characterizing the object and implying an action toward it, thus serving as motive.
substance_types.burke_paradigm_example: 'Friend' / 'brother' / 'bastard' as substance-assignations; the entire pragmatics of injurious and gratifying speech (GM-02 p.57).
substance_types.dialectical_move: FORWARD-ANCHORS the consubstantiation apparatus of *A Rhetoric of Motives* (1950); shows that substantiation is observable structural reality. **Load-bearing seed for the incorporation↔consubstantiation bridge to Calleja.**

substance_types.label: Centrality-of-substance (the synopsis-claim)
substance_types.gloss: Burke's closing thesis: even if substance dissolves under sustained scrutiny, it re-forms as soon as scrutiny relaxes; things do have intrinsic natures, and the quandaries crowd in only when we attempt to fix them definitively. The pentad is therefore 'a philosopher's stone for the synopsis of writings that have sought' it.
substance_types.burke_paradigm_example: Chapter close — the meta-statement that all theology, metaphysics, philosophy, criticism, poetry, drama, fiction, political exhortation involve substance-tactics (GM-02 pp.55-58).
substance_types.dialectical_move: Recapitulates the chapter as a meta-apparatus — every substance-type is a way of stabilizing motive-ascription; the chapter as a whole is a topography of those ways.
